_note: Voice script for Unlikely Heroes. id = file name in audio/voice/. Text in [brackets] is a delivery tag for the voice model and is not shown in subtitles.
intro: [softly] High above the clouds, past the last weather station, floats a city called Skyharbor.
It has docks for airships, gardens on its rooftops, and, way out on its very edge, a junkyard.
[warmly] This is where Vesk lives. Retired mechanic. Professional grump. Owner of one very comfortable chair.
[sighs contentedly] Finally. Nothing left to fix.
Vesk! Vesk, Vesk, Vesk. I alphabetized the scrap pile. Wanna see? It's mostly S. For scrap.
[flatly] Dodger. It's my day off. Every day is my day off. That's what retired means.
[mysteriously] And then, at the exact same moment, on every planet in the galaxy, something switched on.
[nervous] Uh. Why is the toaster growling?
Every bot, everywhere, went completely haywire.
[excited] There's a signal! Some kind of broadcast. It's coming from somewhere in Skyharbor!
A roller bot just ate your chair.
[long pause, then annoyed] ...Fine. Let's go unplug it.
story: Bots! On OUR dock! Somebody left the haywire on.
[sighs] I just wanted one quiet day.
Dock's clear! The signal's coming from further in. Also, Gizmart is open.
[whispering] We are a little bit shopping.
Terraces ahead. Hop the gaps, and try not to fall off the sky this time.
See those rings? Grab one with your hook and swing. Like a monkey. A grumpy monkey.
Cargo docks. Lots of boxes. Some of them have sprockets in them. Smash responsibly.
The signal is stronger up on that tower. Rail's open.
There! A relay dish on top of the mast. That thing is boosting the signal. Scrap it!
Relay scrapped! Ten out of ten! Okay, nine.
Relay's down. The signal is still coming from somewhere else.
Later problem. The Crane Yard is down that rail.
Roof gardens. Pretty flowers, angry bots. Watch your step.
[nervous] Uh, Vesk? That crane is looking at us.
Cranes do not look at people.
It's getting mad! Watch out, it's calling its work crew!
Checkpoint! If you fall off the sky, you start here. Not that you would. Again.
[groans] I'm getting too old for this.
outro: The Crane Yard. A few minutes, and one very large explosion, later.
Crane Bot: scrapped. I'd rate that a nine.
You missed the landing. I'm a professional, Vesk.
[ominously] Then, from somewhere deep inside the wreck, a radio crackled to life.
Every planet will be one big factory. No breaks. No weekends. No exceptions.
This is Foreman Grudd. End of message.
[long sigh] A giant robot foreman. Of course.
[excited] The signal leads off-world. You know what that means!
[warmly] And so, very much against his will, Vesk's adventure had only just begun.
skyharbor: Vesk! Up here! I'm fine. My rotor is not fine. My rotor is a pretzel.
[flatly] You flew into the scrap pile again.
The scrap pile flew into ME. Also, bots incoming. Use the wrench!
They're taking apart your fence! Wrench them, wrench them!
Yard's clear! Now whack my launch crank. Gently. Okay, not gently. It's stuck.
[whooshing] I'm up! I'm up! Flight systems: six out of ten. Rattly.
Gate's open. Let's find whoever is broadcasting and tell them to stop.
The Dock Plaza is across the pads. Hop, hop, don't fall.
The dock turbines are dead. No wind, no cargo lift. The docks are east.
The rail to the far piers is live! Jump on and grind.
Three turbines. Restart them and the lift runs again.
A container canyon! Stay close, Vesk. Get lost in here and they'll ship you to the wrong planet.
[grumbling] Wouldn't be the worst thing that happened to me this week.
Conveyor belts. Grudd loves these. Things that move, so he never has to.
[dry] That belt runs away from the button. Course it does.
[satisfied] There. Line two runs uphill now. Hop on.
[awed] Look at the size of that freighter! I could live in one of its rivets. Comfortably.
Turbine switches! Give each one a good whack. Your favorite repair method.
All three spinning! The cargo lift has power. That's our ride home.
[quietly] The turbine crew walked off mid-shift. Same minute as the toaster. Same signal.
Every bot heard it. So, the Signal Mast. Climb the Terrace, west of the plaza.
Those ledges are too high for you, old man. Jump, then jump again with the jetpack.
Nice. Big gap ahead. Double jump, then hold it to glide. Like a very grumpy kite.
Gardens clear! The promenade leads to the mast. And that bounce pad is the express to the plaza.
[excited] We're on the mast! Somebody cut the ladder halfway up. Ledges, then the catwalk east. The long way!
Relay pylon! Grudd's crews are guarding the lift. Why is it always the lift?
[cheerful] Lift's clear! Ride it up and swing over to the dish. I'll fly. Because I can fly.
[alarmed] Whoa, wind! Get behind a baffle! Not behind me, I'm tiny!
[gruffly] I've been blown around by worse. Mostly by you.
There's the relay dish. It's pointed at nothing. Turn the cranks and line it up!
Aim it right and we'll hear where the signal comes from.
Dish aligned! Picking up the broadcast. There's something hidden in it.
[glitchy, distracted] Inspection log... uh. Sorry. Static. It's a string of numbers. A piece of a code.
Did it? Huh. Seven out of ten, good look. Anyway, the rail to the Crane Yard is open.
One shard of a code. Nana Quill can read it. After the crane.
The Crane Yard gate. Work crews, lined up in threes. Very organized. Very rude.
And look, another Gizmart. He gets everywhere.
Stock up. Something big is moving in there.
terrace: [excited] A tea house! Vesk, look, there's a sign about me. I'm famous! Banned, but famous.
[gruff] Finally. Somebody in this city with standards.
Jump over the fan and hold it. Let the wind do all the work. You know, like you do with everything.
[grumbling] Wind chimes. Great. A headache, now in brass.
[curious] Somebody's laundry. Somebody with very, very small socks.
cutscene: [confused] Uh, Vesk? Did your coffee maker just punch a time card?
[flatly] No. I'm retired. The coffee maker is retired.
[nervous] It's wearing a tiny hard hat.
[zooming away] Follow me! I know a shortcut over the scrap pi- [crash] Ow!
Hop the junk wall! Tap jump. Hold it to go higher.
[booming, crackly radio] Attention, all units! Shift starts NOW. Hard hats on!
[quietly] Dodger. Your eye's doing the orange thing again.
[glitchy] Shift start... logged. Uh. Static! Just static. Rude static.
[crackly radio, warm] Hello? Hello, dear? Is this the fellow from the junkyard with the chatty drone?
Nana Quill. Codebreaker, retired. I've been listening to that broadcast, and your little shard is a set of coordinates.
A desert mining canyon called Dustvein Gulch. I'm sending them to your ship now. Wear a hat, dear. It's sunny.
How did you get this frequency?
[rattling] Liftoff: six out of ten. You forgot the handbrake.
gardens: [amazed] A glass bubble full of fish! Somebody up here really hates windows that open.
[grumbling] Smells like wet socks and roses.
[flatly] A tree. Growing out of the sky. Sure. Why not.
[excited] Look at that view! You can see your junkyard from here! ...It still looks like a junkyard.
[yelling] I am too old for vines!
[whispering] Pollinator drones. Don't make eye contact. They only respect flowers.
[curious] That gardening bot hasn't gone haywire. Probably too busy judging your boots.
[nervous] A rope bridge, way up here. Cool. I'll just hover. Like I always do. Because I'm smart.
cinematics: [warmly] Every morning in Skyharbor starts the same way. The airships hum, the gulls complain, and the bots get to work.
[sips coffee, satisfied] Mm. Not too hot. Not too cold. Not too anything.
Vesk! There's a lady at the gate. She says her lawn bot is eating her lawn.
The sign says, quote: Keep out. I mean it. V.
[distant, echoing, slow and booming] Clock. In.
[nervous] Why is the mail bot wearing a hard hat? Mail bots don't wear hard hats!
[cheerful, smug] Clock in? Ha! I'm self-employed! Nobody tells ME when to clock in!
[fast salesman patter] Hard hats, though? Two for one! Today only! Some restrictions apply!
Whoa, whoa! The dish is projecting something. Is that a face? That is a very square face.
[booming, cheerful announcer voice] Good morning, Skyharbor! This is your new Foreman speaking!
You may have noticed your appliances clocking in. Do not be alarmed. That is called PRODUCTIVITY.
As of today, this city is a work site. Hard hats are mandatory. Smiling is optional. Breaks are... [laughs heartily] no.
Today's motivational quote: TEAMWORK. Because you have no choice.
This has been Foreman Grudd. Employee of the Month. Every month. Back to work!
[flat, robotic monotone] Broadcast received. Shift schedule logged. [normal, startled] Huh? What? Who said that?
So. Giant robot boss guy with a chimney hat. You know him?
[long pause, quietly] ...Lots of foremen out there.
Also! There's a code buried in that signal. One little shard of it. I'm keeping it. For science.
[grumbling] Rail's open. Crane Yard. Let's go unplug something.
[whispering] Okay. Big empty yard. One big empty spot, right in the middle. Totally normal.
[low] Nobody leaves a spot that empty. Something's parking there.
[crackly loudspeaker] Crane Unit Seven! You have a visitor. Please lift him somewhere very high... and let go.
Rating this plan: zero out of ten. Do NOT let go!
[cracks knuckles, grumbling] I'm retired, you know.
[panicking] Great! Tell HIM that! Loudly! While dodging!
[crackly radio] Crane Unit Seven, report. ...Unit Seven? Why is your time card blank?
[sputtering, outraged] Scrapped?! By WHO? That crane was Employee of the Week!
[dry] He talks a lot for a guy with a chimney on his head.
[playful, hushed] Meanwhile, very far away, in an office with no windows and a great many posters...
[slowly, to himself, brooding] Unit Seven. Scrapped. By one retired mechanic... and a talking lightbulb.
[pause, intrigued, quiet] A mechanic. Hm. Hm hm hm.
[booming into an intercom] Print the posters! We're HIRING!
[excited, Saturday morning cartoon announcer] Next time, on Unlikely Heroes: Dustvein Gulch! Sand, scrap pirates, and absolutely no retirement!

spawn: Hey, bolt-brains! Over here! No, the other over here!
Incoming bots. Try to look busy.
More of them? Somebody's factory is working overtime.
Rust buckets at twelve o'clock. Also two, four and nine.
Oh good, a crowd. I love an audience.
taunt: You call that rolling? My grandma had better bearings!
Nice paint job. Did a toaster pick it?
I've seen scarier vending machines. Actually, I know one.
hurt: Ow! I mean, you. Ow for you.
Maybe try being somewhere else when they shoot?
low: Vesk, your hull is held together by spite.
We are VERY low on hull. Like, worryingly.
Grab a green cell before I have to write your eulogy.
fall: That was the sky. We don't stand on the sky.
Back to the checkpoint. I won't tell anyone.
grind: Rail ride! Keep your arms inside the drone.
far: Sniped it. Okay, that was good.
comboEnd: Combo over. It was beautiful while it lasted.
And the streak ends. Bonus sprockets, though.
rate: Wow. A shot. Three out of ten.
Five out of ten. Points for effort.
Seven out of ten. Not bad, old man.
Okay, that was an eight. Don't let it go to your head.
Nine out of ten! I'm telling everyone!
[shouting] TEN OUT OF TEN! Okay, nine. No, ten!
levelup: [excited] Ooh, your blaster just went up a level! It looks so shiny and dangerous!
[cheering] Level up! I'm putting that in my scrapbook!
[impressed] Whoa. It's humming. Is it supposed to hum? I like the hum.
washer: [gasps] A Lucky Washer! That's the luckiest kind of washer!
[delighted] Ooh, shiny! Gizmart trades those for the good stuff!
[whispering] Lucky Washer. Pocket it before somebody sees.
page: [curious] A pink slip? It's got Foreman Grudd's stamp on it. Huh.
[reading slowly] 'Your position has been... discontinued.' Ouch. Who wrote this?

empty: [grumbling] Empty. Somebody find me a crate.
[flatly] Click. That's the sound of bad planning.
levelup: [satisfied] Now we are talking. Mostly to myself.
[dry] Tuned it up. Like riding a bike. A bike that shoots.

hello: Welcome, welcome, valued customer! Gizmart has everything a hero needs!
[cheerful] Ding ding! A shopper! Step right up!
Back again? I knew you couldn't resist my selection!
buy: A fine purchase! Your sprockets are safe with me. Forever.
poor: [sympathetic] Ooh, not enough sprockets. Go smash some bots and come back!
Sorry, friend. Gizmart does not do credit.
bye: Come back soon, and bring sprockets!
Thank you for shopping at Gizmart! Have a haywire-free day!
